overview.rule: When a creature drops to 0 hp or less, it becomes unconscious and may be dead.
Its actual condition is not determined until an ally treats its wounds.
An ally may treat the creature by applying healing magic or by being within 5' and spending an action instead of attacking to apply aid.
Once treated, the creature rolls 1d20+1d6 on the Mortal Wounds table for the damage type that reduced it to 0 hp or less.
The modified 1d20 determines condition and recovery. The modified 1d6 determines the permanent wound suffered.
If the creature is not treated within 24 hours, it rolls with no treatment bonus and with the full -10 penalty for treatment more than 1 day late.
Healing magic used for treatment does not restore hp. It only adds its bonus to the Mortal Wounds roll.
If the condition result is mortally wounded, grievously wounded, or critically wounded, the creature remains at its current hp and must still be healed to 1 hp within the listed time or die.
If the condition result is shocked, knocked out, or dazed, the creature recovers to 1 hp. Further healing then works normally.

modifiers.modifier: Apply the unconscious creature's CON modifier to the d20 roll.
+2 if HD Value 1 (1d6 HD); +4 if HD Value 2 (1d8 HD); +6 if HD Value 3 (1d10 HD); +8 if HD Value 4 (1d12 HD).
+5 if hp are exactly 0; -2 if hp are negative from 1/4 to 1/2 max hp; -5 if hp are negative from 1/2 to max hp; -10 if hp are negative from max to 2x max hp; -20 if hp are negative beyond 2x max hp.

overview.rule: If a creature suffers a permanent wound, repair permanent wound, restore life and limb, regeneration, a ring of regeneration, or similar magic can heal the wound.
If a creature is killed, restore life and limb, reincarnation, or similar magic that restores the dead to life can revive it.
Creatures healed or restored in these ways often require long recovery and may suffer permanent side effects.
Roll 1d20+1d6 on the Tampering with Mortality table matching the creature's alignment.
The modified 1d20 determines the restoration condition and recovery period. The modified 1d6 determines the side effect.
Side effects are permanent and can only be removed with wish.

modifiers.modifier: +2 if youthful; 0 if adult; -5 if middle aged; -10 if old; -20 if ancient.
+1/2 caster level of spellcaster; +2 if cast in the temple of the spellcaster's god.
-10 if instantly killed; -5 per spine severing; -2 per limb destroyed; -1 per hand, foot, ear, eye, tongue, or genitalia destroyed.
Apply creature's WIS modifier; -1 for each full day dead; -1 for each side effect already suffered.
modifiers.rule: The maximum penalty for state of the creature's body is -10.
For state of body, "instantly killed" includes death by disease or poison, being slain while helpless, or rolling instantly killed on the Mortal Wounds table.
Other modifiers from race, class, spells, and items may apply to the d20 or d6 roll.

bed_rest.rule: Some Mortal Wounds and Tampering with Mortality results require bed rest.
During bed rest, the creature is capped at 1 hp.
During bed rest, the creature cannot gain hp from natural or magical healing.
During bed rest, the creature cannot take actions other than speaking and moving at half speed.
If the character is killed again before completing the required rest, the character cannot be treated or restored to life by anything less than ritual magic.
Magical healing can shorten recovery from mortal wounds by 1 day per day (BHR) of healing applied.
Shortening recovery from mortal wounds risks side effects from tampering with mortality.

procedure.name: shortened_mortal_wound_recovery
procedure.step: When the character finishes recovering, roll 1d20+20.
Subtract the number of days by which healing magic shortened the recovery time.
If the total is 20 or less, roll 1d6 and consult the appropriate alignment-based Tampering with Mortality table.
Cross-index the d20 total and d6 total to determine the side effect suffered.

bed_rest.rule: Magical healing cannot shorten recovery from tampering with mortality because that exhaustion is spiritual rather than physical.

confidence_notes.note: Several table cells in the uploaded HTML are OCR-corrupted or merged across adjacent columns. I preserved the recoverable mechanics and normalized obviously intended table structure, but the following entries are below 0.90 confidence: some lawful, neutral, and chaotic tampering table cells at d6 rows 1, 4, 5, and 6; several corpse-condition cells in the fatal-result columns; and a few savage/fire row cells where descriptive text appears split across neighboring columns.
I normalized the attack-type label "savage" from OCR text reading "s aVage"; confidence is high that this is the intended label for tooth-and-claw mauling wounds.

I treated flavor-only death narration as compressed body-condition summaries where that seemed mechanically relevant to later resurrection penalties. Exact prose wording for those fatal cells was intentionally omitted.
